summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 69 (FUSE/WinFsp Rust port with grant-root awareness) of the CipherBox GSD workflow — port TS rotation/scope/listing logic into Rust crates, close crypto revocation gaps, and get a Windows CI/WinFsp plan in place, running end-to-end from planning through wave-based parallel execution with minimal human intervention.
summary.outcome: Planning completed for all 14 plans across 7 waves (research, validation, pattern-mapping, plan-checker all passed, committed at 23b4ba198), and execution proceeded through Wave 5 (10/14 plans merged, cargo green throughout) before halting at a genuine architectural blocker: plan 69-09 discovered the FUSE write path was never migrated off legacy ECIES-wrapped types, invalidating the planned read-path swap and the downstream 69-10 clean cutover; the orchestrator correctly stopped rather than risk a broken build, merged the independent 69-11/69-12 sdk work first, and prepared to report replan options.

repo: GSD commit helper has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` even when lint-staged completes cleanly and the commit lands — always verify via `git log` before retrying.

gsd-tools' API-SURFACE regen (`intel` plan:pre hook) is TS/JS-focused and returns `symbolCount: 0, stale: true` for Rust-only phases — expected, safe to omit from planner prompts when RESEARCH.md already has verified symbol locations.

Fresh git worktrees spawned for executor agents lack `node_modules`, so the husky pre-commit hook fails on first commit (`lint-staged` not found) until `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is run — happened repeatedly across 69-02, 69-04, etc.

Worktree agents' self-reported `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` can be a mis-capture (e.g. 69-06 reported its own docs commit as the base) — always verify the true fork base via `git merge-base` before merging.
`crates/api-client`'s `/shares/sent` endpoint (`SentShareResponseDto`) has no `revoked`/status field because shares are hard-deleted on revoke — every returned row is inherently an active grant.
The desktop E2E GitHub Actions workflow is actually named "Desktop E2E Tests", not "CI E2E Tests" as ROADMAP/CONTEXT docs word it — `gh workflow run "CI E2E Tests"` would 404.
`crates/core`'s `build_node_aad` fail-closes on non-UUID node IDs, which repeatedly tripped test fixtures across multiple plans (69-06, 69-08) until real UUIDv5 strings were used.

Running `rustfmt` from a crate root inside a worktree can reformat unrelated files as a side effect — must be checked/reverted via `git status --short` scope checks before committing (caught in 69-08).

FUSE write-path (`write_ops/implementation/{mkdir,upload,delete,rename}.rs`) has never been migrated to produce Node v3/SealedChildRef-shaped symmetric-sealed data — there is no symmetric per-folder read-key hierarchy to unwrap against yet, blocking any partial ECIES→symmetric read-path swap.

The ECIES call sites planned for swap-out in `inode.rs`/`replay.rs`/`content_ops.rs` are reached from ~9 additional crates/fuse files (fs.rs, read_ops.rs, dir_ops.rs, cache.rs, events.rs, poll.rs, operations.rs, plus 3 platform/windows/*.rs) not covered by plan 69-09's scope.

code.finding: rotate_one takes parent_read_key as &[u8] (a borrow) specifically so the type system — not just convention — prevents zeroing the caller's buffer; read_key_prime is only zeroed on rotate_one's own failure paths.
has_covering_grant/maybe_rotate_on_scope_exit ported from TS scope.ts; 16 tests include the SC#4/ROT-02 zero-rotation invariant and T-63-17 anti-malicious-relay cross-check.

resolve_published_node is pub(crate) only (D-05/SC#6 single gated entrypoint); cold-child gating must source generation/version_floor from the parent SealedChildRef mirror, never the child's own PublishedNode.generation (Pitfall 4/M1).

workflow: When a subagent (planner) crashes mid-response after writing files to disk, verify actual disk state (frontmatter validity, completeness, requirements coverage) before deciding whether to resume vs. restart — resuming preserves context and avoids redoing completed work.
For unattended/`--auto` multi-wave execution, canary the first plan synchronously to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline before fanning out later waves in parallel.
When two plans in the same wave touch a shared file (e.g. both edit crates/sdk/src/lib.rs), serialize them instead of running in parallel to avoid merge conflicts.
Write a durable handoff file to a scratchpad path before pausing/scheduling a resume, so state survives context summarization across the gap.

When an executor agent hits a Rule 4 architectural blocker (assumptions in the plan don't hold against live code), it should stop and document rather than attempt a risky partial rewrite — this correctly happened for 69-09.

After a plan surfaces a blocker that invalidates downstream plans, re-scan remaining queued plans for ones that are still independently valid (e.g. 69-12 depended only on merged 69-03/69-11, not on the blocked FUSE work) rather than halting the entire remaining wave.

friction: Planner agent crashed with a mid-response API/connection error while writing the final plan (69-14), requiring manual disk-state verification and recovery via a fresh single-plan planner spawn.
GSD commit helper repeatedly reports false-negative `commit_failed` even when commits land cleanly, requiring manual `git log` verification each time.

Worktree agents' self-reported `expected_base` metadata can be wrong (mis-captured as the agent's own later commit), requiring manual `git merge-base` verification before every merge to avoid a bad merge.
Fresh worktrees lack `node_modules`, causing husky/lint-staged pre-commit failures on first commit in nearly every spawned executor.

Plan 69-09 revealed a fundamental planning gap: the plan assumed the FUSE write path already produced Node v3/SealedChildRef data, but it never had been migrated, invalidating both 69-09's read-path swap and 69-10's planned legacy-type deletion — a costly discovery only made during execution, not planning/verification.
open_items: Phase 69 execution halted after Wave 5 (10/14 plans merged: 69-01→08, 69-11, 69-12); plans 69-09 (partial), 69-10, 69-13, 69-14 remain blocked pending a replan of the FUSE read/write path migration.

69-09's worktree (agent-a8cce22ff1ad4dcdb) is preserved unmerged, containing the completed SC#6 CI grep gate commit plus investigation findings — needs to be incorporated or discarded once replanning resolves the write-path gap.

Need to replan the FUSE ECIES→symmetric cutover to account for ~9 additional crates/fuse files and the fact that the write path must be migrated to emit Node v3/SealedChildRef data before any read-path swap is safe; this also affects 69-10's legacy-type deletion assumptions.
69-06/69-09's SC#6 grep-gate uses a placeholder symbol name per the plan-checker's non-blocking warning — needs confirmation against the real crate-private resolve symbol name at build time.
Blocker state was durably recorded to /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/phase69-exec-blocker.md for handoff, but the actual replan/decision with the user was still pending at transcript end.
